subproblems.title: Support of a current vanishing off a compact set (reused accepted rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support tsupport ω is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

The selected node's assembly uses it for steps 1 and 4 (spt T ⊆ K is compact; spt Γ is compact), and the children segment_current and filling use it as well.
1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0 by hypothesis.
 By (a)–(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.
2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.
3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.

subproblems.title: Every IMRep defines a current (reused accepted dtc_imrep_current)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U of degree n (the frozen contract structure IMRep U n, Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T), Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).

Reused accepted declaration: this is the exact frozen Lean type of an accepted DAG node with this Lean name, shared here by name; its accepted Lean proof recompiles against the frozen contract with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, and the natural-language proof it was accepted under is the argument below. Source: Simon 6.3.1, where formula (‡) is asserted to define a current; the child segment_current uses it to turn the segment IMRep into a 1-current.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; for a covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. Unit orientations have norm at most one. By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then for every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty when n = 0).
2. Measurability. For every continuous n-form ω, the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: θ is measurable (ℕ-valued), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous because it is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
3. θ is integrable over compact sets. Let K be compact with K ⊆ U. Then 1_K θ is μ-integrable: it is measurable, and ∫ 1_K θ dμ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict; integrable_indicator_iff). Write C_K := ∫ 1_K θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞).
4. Integrability of the integrand. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U), and B := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0. By steps 2–3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. Linearity. Define T(ω) := R.action ω for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand for ω + η is the sum of the integrands for ω and η; both are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) (integral_add). The integrand for cω is c times the integrand for ω, so T(cω) = cT(ω) (integral_const_mul). Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), and R.Represents T holds by definition.
6. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every derivative converges uniformly on K. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖ and D⁰0 = 0) this says ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·C_K (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with step 3). Given ε > 0, choose N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/(C_K + 1) for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. Then |T(ω_j)| ≤ εC_K/(C_K + 1) < ε for j ≥ N, so T(ω_j) → 0.
7. By steps 5 and 6, T is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations satisfy |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for a.e. x in M.
For a test form ω the integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{spt ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ; hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0, so T is a current.

subproblems.statement: (a) For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity. (b) For all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, currents A, B, C ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and integers p, q with A(ω) = p·B(ω) + q·C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), one has M_W(A) ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C) in [0, ∞] for every W ⊆ ℝ^P. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (Euclidean coefficient norm), and M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). (c) Assume (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity. Then for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every type ι, finite set F ⊆ ι, currents S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (i ∈ ι) that are integer multiplicity for i ∈ F, and integers m_i (i ∈ ι), there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_i·S_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{i∈F} |m_i|·M_W(S_i) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.

Source: the selected proof's step 0(ii) (the zero current is IM via the empty IMRep; with (IMC)(c), A + B := A − (0 − B) and all integer combinations of IM currents are IM) and step 0(iii) (masses are subadditive); Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(1) and 2.4–2.5 (definition of M_W). Call ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) W-admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W); then M_W(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over W-admissible ω.
1. (a) Let R be the IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity ≡ 0 and orientation ≡ 0. Its fields hold: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ U; ∅ is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, since μHE[n] ∅ = 0); a constant multiplicity is measurable and positivity on ∅ is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} θ dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞; a constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; and μHE[n].restrict ∅ = 0, so the a.e. orientation condition holds trivially. For every ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_∅ … dHⁿ = 0 = 0(ω). So R represents 0 and 0 is integer multiplicity.
2. A symmetric bound. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and let ω be W-admissible. Then −ω is W-admissible, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω (tsupport_neg) and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). Since X(−ω) = −X(ω) (linearity), ofReal|X(ω)| equals ofReal(X(ω)) or ofReal(X(−ω)), and both are ≤ M_W(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Hence ofReal|X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X).
3. (b) Let ω be W-admissible. Then A(ω) = pB(ω) + qC(ω) ≤ |p||B(ω)| + |q||C(ω)|. By monotonicity of ofReal, ofReal_add (both summands are ≥ 0) and ofReal_mul, ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ ofReal|p|·ofReal|B(ω)| + ofReal|q|·ofReal|C(ω)| ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C), using step 2 and ofReal|p| = (p.natAbs : [0, ∞]) (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, Nat.cast_natAbs, Int.cast_abs). Taking the supremum over ω (sSup_le) proves (b). In particular, with A = B = C = 0 and p = q = 0, M_W(0) = 0.
4. (c), integer multiples. Assume (IMC)(c), let U be open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity. By induction on k ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity V_k with V_k(ω) = k·X(ω) for all ω and M_W(V_k) ≤ k·M_W(X) for all W: V_0 := 0 (integer multiplicity by (a), M_W(0) = 0 by step 3); V_{k+1} := V_k − (0 − X), which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) applied to 0 and X and then to V_k and 0 − X, has values V_k(ω) − (0 − X(ω)) = (k+1)X(ω), and, since V_{k+1}(ω) = 1·V_k(ω) + 1·X(ω), satisfies M_W(V_{k+1}) ≤ M_W(V_k) + M_W(X) ≤ (k+1)M_W(X) by (b). For m ∈ ℤ: if m = |m| take V := V_{|m|}; if m = −|m| take V := 0 − V_{|m|}, which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c), has V(ω) = −|m|X(ω) = mX(ω) and, by (b) with (p, q) = (−1, 0), M_W(V) ≤ M_W(V_{|m|}) ≤ |m|M_W(X). So for every m ∈ ℤ there is an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m·X(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m|·M_W(X) for all ω, W.
5. (c), induction on the finite set F (Finset.induction_on). If F = ∅, Y := 0 works: it is integer multiplicity by (a), Y(ω) = 0 is the empty sum, and M_W(Y) = 0 by step 3. If F' = F ∪ {j} with j ∉ F and S_i integer multiplicity for i ∈ F', the induction hypothesis gives Y_F for F, and step 4 gives an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m_jS_j(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m_j|M_W(S_j). Put Y := Y_F − (0 − V): it is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) twice; Y(ω) = Y_F(ω) + V(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_iS_i(ω) + m_jS_j(ω) = Σ_{i∈F'} m_iS_i(ω) (Finset.sum_insert); and by (b) with p = q = 1, M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(Y_F) + M_W(V) ≤ Σ_{i∈F}|m_i|M_W(S_i) + |m_j|M_W(S_j) = Σ_{i∈F'}|m_i|M_W(S_i). ∎
proof_key_steps: The IMRep with empty carrier represents the zero current.

1. Representations. Apply (REP) with U := ℝ^P to T, ∂T, Y and ∂Y (they have locally finite mass). This gives (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) with measures finite on compact sets, a.e. strongly measurable fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x (hence a.e.), and T(ω) = ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T, ∂T(η) = ∫ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T}, Y(ω) = ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y, ∂Y(η) = ∫ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}. 2. Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of T − Y and ∂(T − Y), and let f be L-Lipschitz; E_t is Borel for every t because f is continuous.
3. The integer slice property of T, applied to (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f, L, gives a null set N_T such that for t ∉ N_T every pair of currents satisfying the slice formulas for these representations has integer multiplicity ∂A − B; likewise the property of Y gives a null set N_Y. 5. Linearity of restrictions. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = T(ω) = (T − Y)(ω) + Y(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ + ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y. For every η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ∂T(η) = T(dη) = (T − Y)(dη) + Y(dη) = ∂(T − Y)(η) + ∂Y(η), so (RU) with k := d and the triples (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ', ξ'), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) gives ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T} = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' + ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}.

Hence for every η, (∂A − B)(η) = A(dη) − B(η) = [A^T_t(dη) − B^T_t(η)] − [A^Y_t(dη) − B^Y_t(η)], i.e. ∂A − B = (∂A^T_t − B^T_t) − (∂A^Y_t − B^Y_t) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

Source: the selected proof's step 5 (V4(i)), with all details supplied; Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(2)–(3) for the slicing identity behind (SL). The selected proof also assumes that X and ∂X have locally finite mass; this is not needed, because the IMRep measures used below are finite on compact sets. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.) Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(X) := X.massOn W.
Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X and ∂X, and let f be L-Lipschitz. Then f is continuous and E_t := {f < t} is a Borel set for every t (measurableSet_lt).
1. Slices. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (open), k := d, T := X and μ, μ', ξ, ξ', f, L; its hypotheses are exactly the admissibility assumptions (finiteness on compact subsets, a.e. strong measurability, a.e. bounds, the two representation formulas) and the Lipschitz property. It yields currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all test forms, such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies M_G(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open G and every t.
2. Z_t has locally finite mass for a.e. t. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and apply (MM) with the constant sequence μ_j := μ, G := B_k(0) (open ball), (a, b) := (−m, m), L, and Z_j(t) := M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) for all j. Its hypotheses hold: f is continuous; μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ(B̄_k(0)) < ∞ since closed balls are compact; and for t ∈ (−m, m), Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_h h⁻¹μ(B_k(0) ∩ {t−h<f<t}) by step 1. (MM) gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m) and ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}). The sequences are constant, so liminf_j Z_j(t) = M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) and the bound is L·μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}) < ∞ (Filter.liminf_const). A measurable function with finite integral over (−m, m) is finite a.e. there (ae_lt_top for volume.restrict (−m, m), then ae_restrict_iff'). Hence for a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) ⇒ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞. Intersecting these countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff over m, then over k) and taking m > |t|, we get a Lebesgue-null set N such that M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for all k ∈ ℕ and all t ∉ N. If W is open with compact closure, then W is bounded, W ⊆ B_k(0) for some k, and M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for t ∉ N (massOn_mono). Fix t ∉ N for steps 3–8.
3. Integrals against IMRep measures. Let R = (M_R, θ, ζ) be an IMRep in ℝ^P of degree q and ν := R.measure = (H^q⌞M_R) with density θ. (i) For compact K, ν(K) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ K} θ dH^q < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, field locallyIntegrable_mult). (ii) ν ≪ H^q⌞M_R (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous); hence ζ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient, AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac) and, by (IMC)(d), |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and all α (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). (iii) For every Borel E and every q-form ω, ∫_E ζ(ω) dν = ∫_{M_R ∩ E} θ·ζ(ω) dH^q: indeed ν⌞E = ((H^q⌞M_R)⌞E) with density θ (restrict_withDensity) = (H^q⌞(E ∩ M_R)) with density θ (Measure.restrict_restrict), and ∫ h d(λ with density θ) = ∫ θ·h dλ for the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density x ↦ θ(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with f := fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ≥0); no integrability is needed). With E = ℝ^P this gives ∫ ζ(ω) dν = R.action(ω).
4. A_t is integer multiplicity. Let R_X be an IMRep of X. (IMC)(b) with E := E_t (Borel) gives a current A' and an IMRep R' representing A' with carrier M_{R_X} ∩ E_t, multiplicity θ_X and orientation ζ_X. Apply (RU) with k := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (R_X.measure, ζ_X), (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): the finiteness, measurability and bound hypotheses hold by admissibility of (μ, ξ), by step 3(i)(ii), and trivially for the zero measure; the identity ∫ξ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ_X(ω)dR_X.measure + ∫0 d0 holds because both sides equal X(ω) (admissibility; step 3(iii) with E = ℝ^P and R_X.Represents X). (RU) with B := E_t and then step 3(iii) with E := E_t give, for every ω, A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_{E_t} ζ_X(ω) dR_X.measure = ∫_{M_{R_X} ∩ E_t} θ_X ζ_X(ω) dH^{d+1} = R'.action(ω). So R' represents A_t and A_t is integer multiplicity.
5. B_t is integer multiplicity: the same argument with an IMRep R_∂ of ∂X (degree d), the pair (μ', ξ') and (RU) with k := d shows that the IMRep obtained from R_∂ by (IMC)(b) with E := E_t represents B_t.
6. ∂A_t is integer multiplicity. Let W be open with compact closure. (i) M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(closure W) < ∞: for a W-admissible η (tsupport η ⊆ W, |η(x)| ≤ 1), η(x) = 0 for x ∉ closure W, so |ξ'(x)(η(x))| ≤ |η(x)| ≤ 1_{closure W}(x) for μ'-a.e. x, and ofReal(B_t(η)) ≤ ‖∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ'‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} ‖ξ'(η)‖ₑ dμ' ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} 1_{closure W} dμ' ≤ μ'(closure W) (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_indicator_one); take the supremum over η. (ii) M_W(Z_t) < ∞ by step 2. (iii) ∂A_t(η) = 1·Z_t(η) + 1·B_t(η) for every η, so the sibling current_algebra (Lean name cbr_cc_current_algebra), part (b), gives M_W(∂A_t) ≤ M_W(Z_t) + M_W(B_t) < ∞. Now BR(d) with U := ℝ^P and R := A_t (integer multiplicity by step 4) shows that ∂A_t is integer multiplicity.
7. Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) (ℝ^P is open; steps 5 and 6).
8. Conclusion. Let t ∉ N and let A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Then A and A_t, and B and B_t, agree on all test forms, so A = A_t and B = B_t (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and ∂A − B = Z_t is integer multiplicity by step 7. Since N is null, this holds for L¹-a.e. t; as (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') and f were arbitrary, X has the integer slice property. ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) provides slice currents A_t, B_t of X and the liminf bound for M_G(∂A_t − B_t).
(MM) with constant sequences and a countable intersection: for a.e. t, ∂A_t − B_t has locally finite mass.
IMRep measures are admissible and ∫_E ζ dR.measure = ∫_{M∩E} θζ dHⁿ; with (IMC)(b) and (RU) this makes A_t and B_t integer multiplicity.
M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(closure W) and current_algebra (b) give locally finite M(∂A_t); BR(d) makes ∂A_t IM and (IMC)(c) makes ∂A_t − B_t IM.
Any A, B with the slice formulas equal A_t, B_t, so X has the integer slice property.

Source: the selected proof's step 3, case n = 1 (the segment currents [[x₀, x]]); Simon Ch. 6, 2.2 (the current [[M]] of an oriented submanifold) and 3.1. Uses the siblings support_vanish (Lean name rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), imrep_current (dtc_imrep_current) and current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra), parts (a) and (b). Unlike the selected proof, a = b is allowed; then S = 0. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_segment_current, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.)
Case a = b.
1. Take S := 0. It is integer multiplicity by current_algebra (a); ∂0(g) = 0 = g(a)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩; current_algebra (b) with A = B = C = 0 and p = q = 0 gives M(0) = M_{ℝ^P}(0) = 0 < ∞; and 0 vanishes on every test form, so support_vanish (U := ℝ^P, K := {a}) gives spt 0 ⊆ {a} = [a, a] (segment_same).
Case a ≠ b.
2. Parametrization. Let ℓ := |b − a| > 0, τ := ℓ⁻¹(b − a) (so |τ| = 1) and φ(u) := a + uτ (u ∈ ℝ). φ is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P (|φ(u) − φ(v)| = |u − v|), hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding); φ(0) = a and φ(ℓ) = b. Put I := φ((0, ℓ)), the open segment. I is Borel (the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding), and I ⊆ [a, b] because φ(u) = a + (u/ℓ)(b − a) with u/ℓ ∈ [0, 1] (segment_eq_image').
3. H¹ on I. On ℝ, H¹ = μHE[1] is Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, finrank ℝ ℝ = 1). For the isometry φ the push-forward of H¹ is H¹⌞φ(ℝ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure); restricting to I (Measure.restrict_map, and φ⁻¹(I) = (0, ℓ) by injectivity) gives H¹⌞I = φ_#(L¹⌞(0, ℓ)). Consequently H¹(I) = ℓ (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, Real.volume_Ioo) and ∫_I h dH¹ = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} h(a + uτ) du for every function h (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
4. Orientation. Let ζ₀ be the 1-vector α ↦ α(τ), i.e. ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ (fun _ => τ), and Q := span{τ}, a line (finrank_span_singleton). ζ₀ is a unit orientation of Q: the one-element family (τ) is orthonormal (|τ| = 1), its span is Q, and ζ₀(α) = α(τ) (IsUnitOrientationOf, first alternative).
5. Approximate tangent line at every point of I. Let x = φ(s₀) with 0 < s₀ < ℓ and δ := min(s₀, ℓ − s₀) > 0. For r > 0, blowUpMap x r sends φ(u) to r⁻¹(u − s₀)τ, so the image of I is contained in Q. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and choose ρ > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_ρ(0). If 0 < r < δ/ρ and y = cτ ∈ Q has f(y) ≠ 0, then |c| = |y| ≤ ρ, so u := s₀ + rc satisfies |u − s₀| ≤ rρ < δ, hence u ∈ (0, ℓ) and y = blowUpMap x r (φ(u)) lies in the image of I. Thus f vanishes on Q ∖ blowUpMap x r '' I, and since Q is closed, ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' I} f dH¹ = ∫_Q f dH¹ for all r ∈ (0, δ/ρ) (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). The integrals are therefore eventually constant in 𝓝[>] 0 and converge to ∫_Q f dH¹; with finrank Q = 1 this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q.
6. The IMRep R := (I, 1, ζ₀) in ℝ^P of degree 1. I is Borel and I ⊆ ℝ^P. I is countably 1-rectifiable: it lies in the range of F(v) := a + v₀τ on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1), which is 1-Lipschitz (|v₀ − w₀| ≤ |v − w|, PiLp.norm_apply_le), since φ(u) = F(EuclideanSpace.single 0 u) (countablyRectifiable_range, CountablyRectifiable.mono). The multiplicity 1 is measurable and positive; ∫⁻_{I∩K} 1 dH¹ ≤ H¹(I) = ℓ < ∞; the constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; and for every x ∈ I (hence H¹⌞I-a.e., ae_restrict_iff') steps 4–5 give Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ₀ Q.
7. By imrep_current there is S ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) represented by R, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_I ω(x)(τ) dH¹(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P). S is integer multiplicity.
8. Boundary. Let g be a test 0-form and ĝ(y) := g(y)⟨⟩. Then g(y) = constOfIsEmpty(ĝ(y)) (a 0-covector is determined by its value on the empty tuple), ĝ is C^∞ (composition of g with the continuous linear evaluation at ⟨⟩), and dg(y) = ofSubsingleton(Dĝ(y)) (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty), so dg(y)(τ) = Dĝ(y)τ. By step 3, ∂S(g) = S(dg) = ∫_I Dĝ(x)τ dH¹ = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} Dĝ(a + uτ)τ du = ∫_0^ℓ Dĝ(a + uτ)τ du (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). By the chain rule u ↦ ĝ(a + uτ) has the continuous derivative Dĝ(a + uτ)τ, so the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt) gives ∂S(g) = ĝ(φ(ℓ)) − ĝ(φ(0)) = g(b)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩.
9. Mass. By (MR) with U = W = ℝ^P, M(S) = M_{ℝ^P}(S) = R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_I 1 dH¹ = H¹(I) = ℓ < ∞.
10. Support. If ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P) has tsupport disjoint from [a, b], then ω(x) = 0 for every x ∈ I ⊆ [a, b], so S(ω) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). [a, b] is compact (the continuous image of [0, 1], segment_eq_image), so support_vanish (U := ℝ^P, K := [a, b]) gives spt S ⊆ [a, b]. ∎
proof_key_steps: a = b: S = 0 (current_algebra (a), (b); support_vanish).
Isometric parametrization φ(u) = a + uτ of the open segment I; H¹⌞I is the image of Lebesgue measure on (0, ℓ).
(I, 1, α ↦ α(τ)) is an IMRep: rectifiable, of finite measure, and every point of I has approximate tangent line ℝτ because blow-ups of I eventually contain ℝτ ∩ spt f.
imrep_current gives the current S; ∂S(g) = ∫_0^ℓ (d/du) g(a + uτ)⟨⟩ du = g(b)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩.
M(S) = H¹(I) < ∞ by (MR); spt S ⊆ [a, b] by support_vanish.

subproblems.title: Compactly supported IM 0-currents are finite integer sums of point evaluations
subproblems.statement: Assume (MR) and (VO). (MR): M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever R is an IMRep representing X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open (verbatim the (MR) hypothesis of the selected node's frozen Lean statement, the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). (VO): S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S (verbatim the (VO) hypothesis of the selected node, the frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support). Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with compact support. Then there are a finite set F ⊆ spt S and integers m(x) (x ∈ ℝ^P) such that S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)·g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g on ℝ^P, where g(x)⟨⟩ denotes the value of the 0-covector g(x) on the empty tuple (fun i => i.elim0).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 0), IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsCompact S.support → ∃ (F : Finset (Euclid P)) (m : Euclid P → ℤ), (↑F : Set (Euclid P)) ⊆ S.support ∧ ∀ g : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 0, S g = ∑ x ∈ F, (m x : ℝ) * (g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the selected proof's step 3, case n = 1 (“H⁰ is the counting measure … so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x); by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ … so ∂T(g) = Σ m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩”), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported integer multiplicity 0-current S. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.)
1. Let R = (M₀, θ, ζ) be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P (degree 0). H⁰ := μHE[0] equals μH[0] (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H⁰(t) = #t for every finite set t (sum_measure_singleton).
2. Carrier points have positive mass: for x ∈ M₀, R.measure({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰⌞M₀ = θ(x)H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton, field mult_pos).
3. M₀ ⊆ spt S. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ spt S; it is the zero region of S, a union of open sets, hence open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G has tsupport disjoint from spt S, so S(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(S) = 0. By (MR) (U = ℝ^P, W = G open), R.measure(G) = M_G(S) = 0. If x ∈ M₀ ∩ G, then R.measure({x}) ≤ R.measure(G) = 0, contradicting step 2. So M₀ ⊆ spt S.
4. M₀ is finite. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set spt S and step 3, ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ < ∞. If M₀ were infinite, then for every N ∈ ℕ there is a finite t ⊆ M₀ with #t = N (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), and N = H⁰(t) = ∫⁻_t 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ (θ ≥ 1 on M₀); so ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ = ∞, a contradiction. Let F be the finite set M₀ (as a Finset).
5. The orientation is ±⟨·⟩ at every carrier point. Let B be the set of x for which no subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M₀ x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ(x)) Q. The field orients says H⁰(B ∩ M₀) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable M₀). Since singletons have H⁰-measure 1, B ∩ M₀ = ∅. So for x ∈ M₀ there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ζ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α or ζ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α; as Fin 0 is empty, τ is the empty tuple ⟨⟩. Hence ζ(x)(α) = s(x)·α(⟨⟩) with s(x) ∈ {1, −1}.
6. Formula. For a test 0-form g, S(g) = R.action(g) = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)ζ(x)(g(x)) dH⁰(x). The integrand is integrable on the finite set M₀, each singleton having finite measure (integrableOn_singleton_iff, integrableOn_finset_iUnion), so ∫_{M₀} h dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈F} H⁰({x})·h(x) = Σ_{x∈F} h(x) (setIntegral_finset). With step 5, S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} s(x)θ(x)·g(x)⟨⟩. Put m(x) := s(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ for x ∈ F and m(x) := 0 otherwise. By step 3, F = M₀ ⊆ spt S. ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] gives mass 1 to every point, so every carrier point has positive R.measure.
(VO) gives M_{ℝ^P∖spt S}(S) = 0, so by (MR) the carrier lies in spt S.
Local integrability of θ ≥ 1 on the compact spt S makes the carrier finite.
The a.e. orientation condition holds at every carrier point, so ζ(x) = ±⟨·⟩.
The integral over the finite carrier is the finite sum S(g) = Σ ±θ(x)g(x)⟨⟩.

subproblems.title: Compactly supported finite-mass IM filling of an IM boundary (V3)
subproblems.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC)(c), (VO) and (ISO). (MR): M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever R is an IMRep representing X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open (verbatim the (MR) hypothesis of the selected node's frozen Lean statement, the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity (the third component of the selected node's (IMC) hypothesis). (VO): S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S (verbatim the (VO) hypothesis of the selected node, the frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support). (ISO) is the conclusion of the frozen statement of the selected node's sibling dependency isoperimetric (Lean name dmcbr_isoperimetric_filling) after its (DT) hypothesis: for all P, m ∈ ℕ there is a real c ≥ 1 such that every integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ equals ∂Y for an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z) and spt Y ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt Z) < 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}}. Let d, P ∈ ℕ and T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with spt T compact, M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂T integer multiplicity. Then there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y compact.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z → IsCompact Z.support → Z.boundary = 0 → Z.mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = Z ∧ Y.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1)) * Z.mass.toReal) ∧ Y.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1))) Z.support) → ∀ (d P : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)), IsCompact T.support → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T.boundary → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = T.boundary ∧ Y.mass < ∞ ∧ IsCompact Y.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the selected proof's step 3 (V3: a compactly supported IM filling Y of ∂T, by the isoperimetric theorem when n = d + 1 ≥ 2 and by signed segments from a point when n = 1, the total multiplicity being zero by (VO)); Simon Ch. 6, 6.1 (isoperimetric theorem) and 8.2 (“the general case of the theorem follows from the special case when ∂T = 0”). Uses the siblings support_vanish (Lean name rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra), segment_current (dmcbr_cc_segment_current) and zero_current_sum (dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum). The selected proof takes the base point x₀ of the segments outside {x_1, …, x_N}; since segment_current also allows coincident endpoints, the base point 0 works in every case (including P = 0 and N = 0). (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_compact_im_filling.)
1. spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact. If η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) has tsupport disjoint from spt T, then tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂T(η) = T(dη) = 0 by (VO). support_vanish with U := ℝ^P and K := spt T (compact) gives spt ∂T ⊆ spt T and spt ∂T compact.
Case d = m + 1 ≥ 1.
2. Z := ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, has compact support (step 1), ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) and M(Z) < ∞. (ISO) with P and m gives c ≥ 1 and an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = Z = ∂T, M(Y) ≤ ofReal(c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z)) < ∞, and spt Y ⊆ thickening(r, spt Z) with r := 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}.
3. spt Y is compact: spt Z is compact, hence bounded, so thickening(r, spt Z) is bounded and its closure C is compact (ℝ^P is proper). If tsupport ω is disjoint from C, it is disjoint from spt Y, so Y(ω) = 0 by (VO); support_vanish with K := C gives that spt Y is compact.
Case d = 0.
4. By step 1 and zero_current_sum (with (MR) and (VO)) applied to the integer multiplicity, compactly supported ∂T ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P), there are a finite F ⊆ spt ∂T and integers m(x) with ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g.
5. Total multiplicity zero: Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0. Choose ρ > 0 with spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) (spt T is compact, hence bounded). Let ψ be a smooth bump function with compact support and ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(0) (ContDiffBump centred at 0 with radii ρ < 2ρ), and let g(y) := constOfIsEmpty(ψ(y)), the 0-form with g(y)⟨⟩ = ψ(y); g is smooth with compact support, so g ∈ 𝒟⁰(ℝ^P). For y ∈ B_ρ(0), ψ = 1 on a neighbourhood of y, so Dψ(y) = 0 and dg(y) = ofSubsingleton(Dψ(y)) = 0 (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty). Hence the support of dg lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), so tsupport(dg) is disjoint from B_ρ(0) ⊇ spt T, and ∂T(g) = T(dg) = 0 by (VO). On the other hand F ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) by step 1, so g(x)⟨⟩ = 1 for x ∈ F and ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x). Hence Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0.
6. Segments. Put a := 0 ∈ ℝ^P. For each x ∈ ℝ^P choose, by segment_current (with (MR)), an integer multiplicity S_x ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with ∂S_x(g) = g(x)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩ for all test 0-forms g, M(S_x) < ∞ and spt S_x ⊆ [a, x].
7. Combination. current_algebra (c), with (IMC)(c), U := ℝ^P (open), ι := ℝ^P, the finite set F, the currents S_x and the integers m(x), gives an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with Y(ω) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(ω) for all ω and M(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F}|m(x)|M(S_x) < ∞ (a finite sum of finite terms).
8. ∂Y = ∂T: for every test 0-form g, ∂Y(g) = Y(dg) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(dg) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)∂S_x(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)g(x)⟨⟩ − (Σ_{x∈F} m(x))g(a)⟨⟩ = ∂T(g) by steps 4–6; hence ∂Y = ∂T (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. spt Y is compact: C := ⋃_{x∈F}[a, x] is compact, being a finite union of segments, each the continuous image of [0, 1]. If tsupport ω ∩ C = ∅, then tsupport ω ∩ spt S_x = ∅ for each x ∈ F, so S_x(ω) = 0 by (VO) and Y(ω) = 0; support_vanish with K := C gives that spt Y is compact.
10. In both cases Y is integer multiplicity, ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt ∂T ⊆ spt T is compact ((VO) and support_vanish).
d ≥ 1: (ISO) applied to the cycle ∂T; the filling lies in a bounded thickening, so its support is compact.
d = 0: ∂T = Σ m(x)δ_x over a finite F ⊆ spt T (zero_current_sum), and Σ m(x) = 0 by testing with a bump form equal to 1 near spt T and (VO).
Y := Σ m(x)[[0, x]] (segment_current, current_algebra (c)) is IM with ∂Y = ∂T, finite mass and compact support.
